---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Enterprise Book Depreciation Conservatism
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), MAX(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))))), SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms cheap on book enterprise value should outperform when current depreciation intensity is above the firm’s recent norm.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This extends the strongest depreciation-conservatism evidence from book-to-market to a broader enterprise-book valuation measure, reducing sensitivity to leverage and excess cash. Cheap capital is more credible when the firm is recognizing asset consumption conservatively rather than inflating earnings through low depreciation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Earnings Yield Depreciation Conservatism
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: High earnings-yield firms should outperform when reported earnings are depressed by unusually conservative depreciation expense.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: A cheap earnings multiple is more attractive when earnings are achieved despite elevated depreciation intensity, not because depreciation expense has been relaxed. The signed depreciation-surprise leg rewards conservative expense recognition and penalizes underdepreciation without using a hard gate.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Net Accrual Conservatism Book
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUB(SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)), RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Book-to-market cheapness should be strongest when conservative depreciation is not offset by operating working-capital accrual buildup.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This nets two accounting-quality channels: conservative depreciation supports value, while positive operating working-capital accruals weaken it. High scores identify cheap book firms where accounting quality is favorable on balance, rather than relying on a single accrual component.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Cash Flow Underdepreciation Reliance Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(MUL(at, SUB(MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3), RATIO(dp, at))), ADD(ABS(oancf), ABS(ib))))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating-cash-flow-yield firms should underperform when current depreciation expense is unusually low relative to the firm’s recent policy.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Cheap cash flow can be misleading if the income component of operating cash flow is supported by understated asset consumption. Scaling the depreciation shortfall by earnings and cash-flow magnitude focuses on cases where underdepreciation is economically meaningful.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Dividend Yield Depreciation Conservatism
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dvc, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUB(RATIO(dp, at), MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: High dividend-yield firms should outperform when payouts are accompanied by conservative depreciation expense recognition.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Dividend yield can be a value trap if payouts are supported by overstated accounting profitability. A positive depreciation-conservatism interaction favors cheap payout stocks whose reported earnings are not being flattered by unusually low depreciation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Rising Depreciation Asset Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(at, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 3))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms cheap relative to total assets should outperform when depreciation intensity is rising over time.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Asset cheapness is more credible when the firm is increasingly recognizing asset consumption, which makes reported earnings and book values less likely to be overstated. The trend construction tests a gradual shift toward conservative accounting rather than a single-year depreciation surprise.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE Enterprise Book Depreciation Conservatism---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The depreciation-surprise leg is byte-identical to the archive's strongest signal (Depreciation Conservatism Book Interaction) and only the value leg is swapped from book/market to book-EV/EV — a third cosmetic variant of the same family after the book and asset-yield versions, with no diagnosis of why the leverage/cash adjustment should matter.

---CRITIQUE Earnings Yield Depreciation Conservatism---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is essentially the sign-mirrored, unscaled twin of the archived "Underdepreciation Earnings Reliance Trap" (same earnings-yield rank leg, same dp/at vs MA(dp/at,3) surprise), and the hypothesis wording is muddled since the value leg uses reported ib, which is mechanically depressed by the very depreciation elevation being rewarded.

---CRITIQUE Net Accrual Conservatism Book---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Netting the depreciation-surprise leg against asset-scaled working-capital accruals is a genuinely new composite that tests whether the accrual channel adds incrementally to the archive's best depreciation result, though there is a real risk the known-strong depreciation leg simply dominates a noisy accrual term that has repeatedly failed in this archive.

---CRITIQUE Cash Flow Underdepreciation Reliance Trap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Internally inconsistent mechanism — operating cash flow adds depreciation back and is essentially invariant to depreciation policy, so "cheap cash flow supported by understated asset consumption" does not follow; it is also just the archived Underdepreciation Earnings Reliance Trap with oancf substituted for ib in the value leg.

---CRITIQUE Dividend Yield Depreciation Conservatism---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Another value-leg swap onto the already-tested depreciation-conservatism interaction, with a weaker link (dividends are a cash payout only loosely tied to depreciation policy) and likely reduced, dividend-payer-only coverage that risks overstating improvement.

---CRITIQUE Rising Depreciation Asset Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: TREND(dp/at,3) is nearly the same information as the archived asset-yield signal's dp/at minus MA(dp/at,3) deviation, making this a smoothing-level cosmetic variant of a signal already evaluated (and the related MA3−MA5 persistence variant already failed).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Enterprise Accrual Claim Book Yield
EXPRESSION: RATIO(ADD(ceq, SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), ADD(MAX(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), MAX(SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp), SUB(at, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Enterprise book cheapness should be strongest when positive total accruals do not create an additional accounting claim on firm value.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This gives the leverage and cash adjustment a substantive role by valuing book capital on an enterprise basis rather than simply swapping the value leg in the depreciation signal. Positive accruals are treated as a shadow claim in the denominator, so firms remain high only when enterprise book cheapness is not supported by accrual buildup.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Depreciation Policy Stability Earnings Yield
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(ib, MUL(at, VOL(RATIO(dp, at), 3))), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
HYPOTHESIS: Earnings-yield cheapness should be rewarded when reported earnings are not produced under an unstable depreciation policy.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This avoids the mechanical issue that high current depreciation depresses the reported earnings-yield numerator. Instead, it penalizes earnings yield for volatility in depreciation intensity, targeting firms whose accounting expense recognition is noisy or potentially discretionary.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Working Capital Release Cash Flow Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, ADD(apalch, ADD(txach, aoloch)))), ADD(ABS(oancf), ABS(sale))))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating-cash-flow-yield firms should underperform when operating cash flow is boosted by broad working-capital releases and accrual financing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This shifts the cash-flow trap away from depreciation policy, since operating cash flow adds depreciation back. Positive cash-flow-statement accrual components indicate temporary cash sources from collections, inventory liquidation, payables, tax accruals, or other operating items, making cheap cash flow less sustainable.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Clean Coverage Dividend Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dvc, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(SUB(dvc, SUB(ib, SUB(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), dp))), ADD(ABS(dvc), ABS(ib))))
HYPOTHESIS: High dividend-yield firms should underperform when dividends exceed accrual-adjusted earnings capacity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This makes the dividend link explicit through clean payout coverage rather than loosely pairing payout yield with depreciation conservatism. High values require both an apparently cheap payout and an accrual-adjusted earnings shortfall, suggesting the dividend yield may be unsustainable.

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Current Asset Quality Asset Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(at, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), ADD(ABS(act), ABS(sale))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms cheap relative to total assets should underperform when asset value is accompanied by receivable and inventory buildup.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This replaces the depreciation-trend variant with an asset-quality mechanism. High asset-to-price firms can be value traps when current assets are swelling through uncollected receivables or inventory accumulation, so the interaction targets cheap assets whose realizability is questionable.
